newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW - CTS sees Dynamics bid superior.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - CTS sees Dynamics bid superior.

text.p: The chief executive officer of CTS Corp said the company's $204 million cash and stock merger agreement with Dynamics Corp represents a better offer than a $171 million hostile bid from WHX Corp.
"We feel this transaction provides more benefits to shareholders than any other proposed transaction," Joseph Walker told Reuters in an interview.
In announcing the friendly transaction, CTS is playing a "white knight" role to Dynamics, which has rejected WHX's hostile offer of $45 per share.
Walker said the union with Dynamics would represent a significant step for CTS, which has spent the past eight years concentrating on internal structure and operations.
CTS also is pursuing other acquisitions and strategic alliances, he said.
"We're looking for growth," he said, noting the company's main focus is automotive, communications and computers.
WHX initially launched a $40 per share offer for Dynamics in late March and then raised its bid to $45 in April. In rejecting the offer, Dynamics had said it was pursuing alternative transactions.
The proposed CTS-Dynamics transaction builds on a 15-year relationship between the two companies. Dynamics holds a 44.1 percent stake in CTS.
WHX had no immediate comment on the transaction.
Walker declined to comment on how CTS would react if WHX raised its offer.
Walker said Dynamics would maintain its Greenwich, Conn., corporate headquarters for now, although it would likely eventually be consolidated with CTS' Elkhart, Ind., headquarters.

Walker did not specifically address potential layoffs from the transaction, saying there would "not be an unusually high amount." He also declined to comment on the proposed transaction's specific impact on earniongs, although the company earlier said the deal would be accretive.
The deal calls for a cash tender for about half of Dynamics' stock for $55 per share. The rest would be swapped in an exchange of 0.88 share of CTS for each Dynamics share.
A spokesman said the proposed transaction does not include a "collar" or other price protection mechanism.
Shares of Dynamics surged 8-7/8 to 53-1/4. CTS shares fell 1-3/8 to 60-3/8 in late morning activity.
